architecture_delta.finding: DB-local V15 lease_epoch is an in-lineage generation fence but is not globally monotone across restoration of an older valid UnifiedDB snapshot. A pre-snapshot capability can become current again after rollback even though SQLite integrity remains valid.
architecture_delta.required_property: Accepted recovery must advance or consult a non-rollback incarnation/restore generation before self.root resumes material operations, or prove an equivalent invalidation mechanism that makes every pre-restore execution/response/effect/handoff capability permanently stale.
candidate_forms: external monotonic incarnation counter outside reverted snapshot
restore-time signed/verified generation bump before runtime readiness
non-rollback host identity epoch plus DB lease epoch composite generation
equivalent recovery authority with formal stale-capability invalidation
architecture_delta.counterhypothesis: If production policy can prove an older snapshot is never restored after any newer execution generation existed, or a separate already-admitted non-rollback authority invalidates all pre-restore capabilities before runtime opens, the demonstrated path may be unreachable in production.
architecture_delta.next_discriminator: Test the actual Frank v0.1 backup/restore/recovery implementation, not only disposable SQLite state. Kill/restart/restore with issued token/request/effect/response/handoff capabilities and require every pre-restore material capability to fail before readiness becomes HEALTHY.

external_primary_support.relevance: Snapshot restore can lower observed revisions; revision bump and compaction are used to prevent stale clients/watches from treating restored old revision space as current. This is an engineering analogy, not proof that Frank should copy etcd implementation.
